extracted.intended_audience: members of the London Mathematical Society; UK and European academic mathematicians (researchers, faculty, postdocs, students)
extracted.subtask_description: Administrative notices, calls, and procedural requirements published in the London Mathematical Society Newsletter (membership business, meetings, fellowships, jobs, library and meeting registration rules). Targets LMS members and the wider mathematical community in the UK/Europe.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual General Meeting — Ballot paper voting procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: A Member of the Society is entitled to vote in the election by striking out on the Ballot Paper those names for which he/she does not vote. The Member must then validate the Ballot Paper both by writing her/his name legibly on it and by signing it. The completed Ballot Paper should either be brought to the AGM or sent to 'The Scrutineers, London Mathematical Society, Burlington House, Piccadilly, London W1V ONL', to arrive at least 36 hours before the time of the AGM. An appropriate envelope is enclosed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ballot paper is enclosed with the Newsletter; procedure for invalidation (strike out) and validation (name + signature) is mandatory; can be delivered in person at the AGM or must reach scrutineers in time (36 hours). Election is governed by Society Charter/Statutes/By-Law I references provided elsewhere in the notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual General Meeting — nomination deadline / uncontested election note
rubrics_metrics.description: The election is uncontested because no nomination from a Member of the Society was received by the Council and General Secretary by the deadline of 1 September 1993.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implicit requirement/criterion: nominations must be received by the Council and General Secretary by the stated deadline to contest elections; absence of nominations leads to uncontested slate recommended by Council under By-Law 1.6.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual Dinner booking requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The 1993 Annual Dinner will be held after the AGM on Friday 19th November. The cost is £21.50 per person and members may book places for guests. The booking form enclosed with this Newsletter should be returned together with payment to the London Mathematical Society office by Wednesday 10th November.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Payment must accompany returned booking form; booking for guests permitted; use enclosed booking form and return to LMS office by specified deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual subscription renewal procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: The annual subscription, including publications, for the session November 1993 - October 1994 is due on 1st November 1993. Together with this Newsletter is a renewal form to be completed and returned with your remittance in the enclosed envelope. No action is required if you are already paying by Direct Debit and do not wish to change your choice of publications. Fully complete and return the form if you are paying by Direct Debit but wish to change the choice of publications or add/delete a subscription to the European Mathematical Society. Bank accounts of members paying by Direct Debit will be debited with the appropriate amount on 17th January 1994. Other members should either enclose a cheque (£ sterling or US$) with their form or, if they have a UK bank account and wish to take advantage of Direct Debit, request a Direct Debit mandate. If the renewal form is missing, write to Miss H.K. Lotay ... or e-mail: lms@uk.ac.kcl.cc.oak.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Action depends on payment method: if already on Direct Debit and no change — no action; if changing publications or Direct Debit choices — return completed form; non-Direct Debit payers must include cheque or request mandate; Direct Debit debit date specified; contact provided if form missing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publications pricing policy — personal use restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: The London Mathematical Society has a pricing structure for its journals which allows individual members to purchase them at a substantial discount. These discounted prices are intended for personal use only and the journals should be kept among your personal belongings and not deposited, even temporarily, in a library, common room or other public area. Issues of the journals should be accessible to other mathematicians or students only with your permission, given individually in each instance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Members must not place discounted personal copies in public/shared collections; access to others should be controlled case-by-case by the member. This is a usage/policy constraint tied to discounted rates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hardy Lecturer — nominations and submission deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: The Council invites members of the Society to submit their views on possible candidates for the 1995 Hardy Lectureship, together with reasons for their choice, confidentially in writing to any member of the General Purposes Committee ... by 30 November 1993.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions should be written, confidential, give reasons for candidate choice, and be sent to named committee members by the stated deadline; background about the lectureship (distinguished overseas mathematician, length of visit, ~twelve lectures) is provided to inform nominations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leibniz Post-Doctoral Fellowships — eligibility conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must be citizens of a member state of the European Community or resident in the Community, be under 33 and expect to have completed a PhD or equivalent degree by 1 October 1994. Exceptionally, consideration may be given to applicants who expect to finish by 1 October 1995. Applicants should propose at least 2 institutions at which they would accept appointment; each of which must be outside their country of citizenship or residence, and other than the institution at which their doctoral studies have been carried out. In all cases successful candidates will be expected to take up their fellowships on 1 October 1994. Holders will be encouraged to spend 6 months at a second network institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict age, citizenship/residency, PhD-completion date expectations; requirement to propose multiple host institutions with constraints (outside home country and not PhD institution); start date is fixed; mobility expectation (visit second network institution for ~6 months). Network institutions are listed for applicant reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leibniz Fellowships — application materials and referees procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications must include a c.v., list of publications, concise description of research interests and the names of 3 referees, and should reach the coordinator by 30 October 1993. Each candidate must ensure that his/her referees send their reports so as to reach the coordinator by the same date. A network committee will make an initial selection of the fellows on 13 November 1993.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete application packet required; referees' reports are mandatory and must meet the same deadline as the application; explicit coordinator contact provided; selection timetable is given (initial selection date).

rubrics_metrics.name: Leibniz Fellowship — coordinator contact and submission address
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications should reach the coordinator Dr. C.B. Thomas, Leibniz Fellows, Department of Pure Mathematics & Mathematical Statistics, University of Cambridge, 16 Mill Lane, Cambridge CB2 1SB (fax: 44-223-337920) by 30 October 1993.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the provided postal/fax contact; ensure referees' reports are also sent to this coordinator by the deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: MSRI membership and fellowship application procedures and deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are interested in applying you should request an application form. Write to MSRI (address given) or send email to: info@msri.org with the single word 'help'. Candidates are asked to make sure that their application materials and letters of reference arrive by the deadline (September 30, 1993 for Research Professorships and November 30, 1993 for the others). Late applications cannot be assured a complete consideration. Awards will be announced by mid-December, 1993 for Research Professorships and by late February, 1994 for the others. Women and minority candidates are especially encouraged to apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the specific request method ('help' email or postal request); adhere to program-specific deadlines for application materials and reference letters; late materials risk incomplete consideration; timeline for announcements provided; affirmative encouragement for underrepresented groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cambridge Professorship of Statistical Science — application requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications are invited for this newly-established Chair, tenable from 1 October 1994. Further information from the Secretary General of the Faculties. Applications (10 copies) with names of two referees by 25 October 1993. The University follows an equal opportunities policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit the specified number of copies and include names of two referees; observe the closing date; equal opportunity statement noted.

rubrics_metrics.name: DPMMS University Lecturer/Assistant Lecturer — application details
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications are invited for this post in any field of Pure Mathematics to take up appointment from 1 October 1994. Further information and details of application procedure can be obtained from the Head, DPMMS ... The closing date for applications is 1 December 1993. Current salary scales are quoted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Field is open within Pure Mathematics; contact department for procedure; observe closing date; salary scale info provided to applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: SERC Research Associate (Arithmetic Geometry and Automorphic Forms) — application details
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications are invited for this 3-year postdoctoral research position, commencing on 1 October 1994 ... Further information and details of application procedure can be obtained ... The closing date for applications is 15 December 1993.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Postdoctoral position with a fixed start date and closing date; contact point provided for details; age-related salary scale noted in listing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Royal Society Discussion Meetings — registration required and contact procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Attendance is open to anyone who is interested, but registration for Discussion Meetings is required. The programme, registration form and other information are available from the Scientific Meetings Secretary, The Royal Society, 6 Carlton House Terrace, London SW1Y 5AG (telephone and extension given).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advance registration is mandatory for Discussion Meetings (even when attendance is open); obtain programme and registration form from the Royal Society contact; telephone contact and extension provided for enquiries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Royal Society Library — access, reference and copying conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Library is open Monday to Friday from 10.00 - 17.00. It welcomes all bona fide researchers, but new enquirers are asked to discuss their requirements with the Librarian, and to supply a reference. A number of catalogues are available; Library staff provide help. Books may be borrowed by some authorized persons, but all loans are at the Librarian’s discretion. Photocopies of manuscripts can be supplied, but only if the copying process does not endanger fragile materials. Readers will normally be provided with microfilm or printed copies of archive material for their research studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Researchers should contact the Librarian and provide references before access; borrowing is restricted and discretionary; preservation considerations may limit copying—microfilm/printed copies are the normal provision for archival material; contact details and scope of collections are given to help researchers plan visits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Job application copy-number and local submission conventions (Leicester Chair example)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications for the Chair of Mathematics at Leicester: UK candidates should submit eleven copies of their application (overseas candidates may submit one copy). Closing date 25 October 1993. Informal enquiries welcome and addressed to named contact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different copy-number conventions may apply for domestic vs overseas applicants — check job notice instructions; informal enquiries are acceptable; observe closing date and equality policy statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conference participation — invitation letter procedure (Third Korean Group Theory Conference)
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are interested in participating in the Third Korean Group Theory Conference and would like to receive a letter of invitation and the second announcement early in 1994, write to Professor Ann Chi Kim (contact details given) or Dr D.L. Johnson (contact details given).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure to request an invitation letter and further announcements provided; use the named contacts/addresses or email for early receipt of documents needed for travel/participation.
